title: add-hpc-frame-counters-and-perfetto-export-for-batching-hotpath
author: Priya Shah
description: Summary: Add high-resolution in-process counters, frame-level tracing scopes and a lightweight Perfetto export hook to the runtime hot-path (continuous batching, scheduler, KV cache) to make microbench timelines reproducible and low-overhead for production-style runs. Motivation: existing NVTX-based instrumentation is useful for ad-hoc GPU traces but lacked fine-grained programmable counters and an easy path to generate deterministic traces for the microbench harness. This PR introduces per-thread frame counters, a compact ring-buffer event sink, and trace export that produces Perfetto-format JSON suitable for timeline viewers and long-running microbench ingestion. Design highlights: 1) hpc::FrameCounters: lock-free, per-core counters for category events (e.g., batch_start, batch_emit, kv_hit, kv_miss, schedule_wait). Counters are aggregate-friendly and exported as delta snapshots. 2) tracing::FrameScope: RAII-style scopes that annotate event boundaries and attach a small integer frame-id to both counters and the trace stream. Scopes are no-op when tracing disabled. 3) perfetto_exporter: modular sink that flushes the in-process ring buffer to a Perfetto-compatible JSON file; supports live stream-to-disk and postmortem dumps. 4) microbench CLI integration: bench/run_trace.sh driver that runs the existing batching microbench with tracing enabled, producing trace artifacts under artifacts/perf/ with metadata for the dashboard. 5) Runtime knobs: rtrace.enable, rtrace.sampling_interval_ms (for low-overhead mode), rtrace.max_events to bound memory. Backwards compatibility: NVTX emissions are preserved behind a feature flag; default remains the new compact exporter when the harness is used. Checklist: - [x] Implement FrameCounters and frame-scoped events - [x] Add perfetto exporter with streaming and file-dump modes - [x] Wire into batching hot-path, scheduler, KV cache hooks - [x] Add microbench driver and example trace artifact - [x] Add unit tests for counters and exporter round-trip - [x] Update runtime flags and docs - [x] Add example dashboard snapshot (Grafana/dash JSON) Testing: unit tests added for counter increment/decrement semantics and ring buffer wrap. Microbench runs were executed in CI perf job (separate job) that validates the exporter output schema and checks event continuity across frames. Manual validation: loaded generated traces into Perfetto UI and validated batch start/end pairing, KV hit/miss counts correlating with microbench config. Commits: - "Add hpc frame counters and API" - implements core counters and aggregator - "Add FrameScope tracer and hook points in batcher/scheduler/kv" - integrates scopes in hot-paths - "Perfetto exporter and microbench driver" - exporter, CLI driver, artifact plumbing - "Tests and dashboard snapshot" - unit tests, perf job, dashboard JSON Changed files (high level): - runtime/src/hpc/frame_counters.cpp/.h - runtime/include/hpc/frame_counters.h - runtime/src/tracing/frame_scope.cpp/.h - runtime/src/scheduler/scheduler_tracing.cpp (hook points) - runtime/src/batcher/continuous_batcher.cpp (scope start/end) - runtime/src/kv/cache_tracing.cpp (kv hit/miss hooks) - bench/microbench/run_trace.sh - bench/microbench/configs/trace_small.yaml - tools/perfetto_exporter/exporter.cpp/.h - docs/perf/tracing.md - observability/dashboards/microbench-batching.json Review thread summary: "Marco Li" (reviewer) 2024-11-06: "Nice low-overhead approach. Two asks: reduce allocation in the ring buffer hot path and add an option to strip event payloads for production runs." Author (Priya) 2024-11-06: "Agree on allocation; switched to preallocated fixed-size segments and added rtrace.strip_payload flag." "Jamal Ortiz" 2024-11-08: "Can we make the sampling_interval_ms default to 0 (off) in hosted to avoid unexpected perf noise? Also suggest exposing counters via /admin/debug/counters for quick inspection." Author 2024-11-08: "Default left as off for hosted; added path to expose delta snapshots under /admin/debug/counters (auth gated)." "Elena Park" 2024-11-10: "Minor: add comment that frame-id wraps at 2^32 and consumer should handle wrap-around." Author 2024-11-10: "Added comment and unit test for wrap behavior." Approvals: Marco Li (APPROVED), Jamal Ortiz (APPROVED after changes), Elena Park (APPROVED). CI: build (green), unit-tests (green), perf-suite (green, flaky tolerances accepted), lint (green). Merge: squash-merge into main on 2024-11-12. Notes: The exporter produces artifact files bundled into the perf job and uploaded to S3 under s3://redwood-perf/artifacts/2024-11-12/pr-23102/. A Grafana dashboard snapshot is included; teams can import microbench-batching.json to visualize frame-level counters alongside existing latency percentiles. Security: no secrets were added, exporter files follow artifact retention policy. Rollout: feature gated behind rtrace.enable; no runtime breaking changes. Release notes: "Add high-resolution runtime frame counters and Perfetto trace export for the continuous-batching hot-path; enables reproducible microbench timelines and low-overhead production tracing."
